1. Install VRCReceiver on your PC and start it (the PC shows a bridge address).
2. Plug the UVC camera into the headset / phone USB port (for multiple cameras use a powered USB hub).
3. Enter the PC LAN IP below, or tap "Auto-detect PC Receiver".
4. Tap "Start Forwarding" and tap Allow on the USB permission dialog.
5. On the PC, copy the stream address shown on the panel into your face/eye-tracking software (e.g. Baballonia, OpenCV-based tools).

Notes:
• Keep the headset and PC on the same LAN.
• Forwarding stops if you exit the app — a persistent notification is shown while running.
• Multiple cameras can be forwarded at once (up to 6) and unplugged devices recover automatically.

Quest users: if a system dialog asks which app to open the USB camera with (a virtual-screen / media app choice), you can choose Don't allow. If it keeps popping up, just close it — it does not affect this app.
VRCForwarder — forward USB UVC cameras (eye/face tracking) from a VR headset or Android phone to a PC over Wi-Fi.\nOpen source (MIT) — free for any use including commercial, attribution required.
